body.p: This listing of claims will replace all prior listings of claims in the application.

br.br:
1. (Currently Amended) A system for touchless control of a lavatory of an aircraft, the system comprising:at least one sensor a plurality of touchless sensors located in the lavatory, wherein each of the plurality of touchless sensors is[[ and]] configured to detect detected receive data corresponding to the lavatory;
at least one anactuator or light source located in the lavatory and configured to perform[[ an]] a first action;[[ and]] a light source located in the lavatory and configured to perform a second action; and
a central controller coupled to the at least one sensor plurality of touchless sensors, and the at least one the actuator, and[[or ]]the light source, the central controller [[and ]]configured to make an inference as to a portion of the lavatory that was used based on the detected data received from each of the plurality of touchless sensors and to control [[the ]]at least one of the actuator [[or ]]and the light source based on the inference.
2. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the at least one sensor includes a touchless sensor configured to receive the data received includes user input corresponding to requested operation of a component of the lavatory[[,]] and the central controller is further configured to control the at least one actuator or thelight source based on the user input.
3. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 2, wherein the at least one plurality of touchless sensors includes:
a touchless seat sensor configured to receive a toilet seat request corresponding to a request to lift a toilet seat of the lavatory;
a touchless lid sensor configured to receive a toilet lid request corresponding to a request to lift a toilet lid of the lavatory;
a touchless soap sensor configured to receive a soap dispense request corresponding to a request to dispense soap within the lavatory;
a touchless faucet sensor configured to detect a faucet request corresponding to a request to operate a faucet of the lavatory;
a touchless flush sensor configured to detect a flush request corresponding to a request to flush a toilet of the lavatory; and
a touchless trash sensor configured to detect a trash flap request corresponding to a request to actuate a trash flap of the lavatory.
4. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 2, further comprising an actuator controller coupled to the at least one of the actuator or thelight source and connected to the central controller, wherein the central controller is configured to control the at least one actuator or the light source by transmitting a control request to the actuator controller.
5. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 2, wherein the at least one actuator or light source includes an ultraviolet light source located in the lavatory [[and ]]configured to emit ultraviolet light having a wavelength that at least one of injures, neutralizes, or kills pathogens, and wherein the central controller is further coupled to the ultraviolet light source and configured to control the ultraviolet light source based on the detected data received.
6. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 5, wherein the at least one actuator or light source further includes a visible light source located in the lavatory and configured to emit visible light having a visible wavelength, wherein the central controller is further configured to control the at least one actuator or the light source to cause a total power draw of the system to remain at or below a power threshold corresponding to a maximum amount of power available to the system.
7. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 6, wherein the central controller is further configured to control the at least one actuator or light source to at least partially operate sequentially to cause the total power draw of the system to remain at or below the power threshold.
8. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 5, wherein the central controller is further configured to determine a health status of the system including at least one of a remaining life of the ultraviolet light source, surface wear experienced by surfaces of the lavatory in response to the ultraviolet light, or a remaining quantity of supplies in the lavatory, and to control at least one of the at least one actuator or the light source further based on the health status.
9. (Original) The system of claim 1, wherein the inference includes at least one of an inferred portion of the lavatory used by a passenger for which sanitization is desirable or whether the lavatory is occupied.
10. (Currently Amended) A system for touchless control of a lavatory of an aircraft, the system comprising:multiple sensors located in the lavatory and each of the multiple sensors is configured to detect detected receive data corresponding to the lavatory;
multiple actuators or light sources located in the lavatory and each configured to perform [[an]] a first action; [[and]] multiple light sources located in the lavatory and each configured to perform a second action;
a central controller coupled to each of the multiple sensors= [[and ]]each of the multiple actuators, and each of the multiple[[ or]] light sources, the central controller[[ and]] configured to make an inference as to a portion of the lavatory that was used for which sanitation is desirable based on the detected data received from each of the multiple sensors and to control at least one ofthe multiple actuators [[or]]and the multiple light sources based on the inference.
11. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 10, wherein:the multiple sensors include:
a touchless seat sensor configured to receive a toilet seat request corresponding to a request to lift a toilet seat of the lavatory,
a touchless lid sensor configured to receive a toilet lid request corresponding to a request to lift a toilet lid of the lavatory;
a touchless soap sensor configured to receive a soap dispense request corresponding to a request to dispense soap within the lavatory,
a touchless faucet sensor configured to detect a faucet request corresponding to a request to operate a faucet of the lavatory,
a touchless flush sensor configured to detect a flush request corresponding to a request to flush a toilet of the lavatory, and
a touchless trash sensor configured to detect a trash flap request corresponding to a request to actuate a trash flap of the lavatory; [[and]] the multiple actuators or light sources include:
a toilet seat actuator configured to actuate the toilet seat,
a soap actuator configured to dispense the soap,
a faucet actuator configured to actuate the faucet,
a trash flap actuator configured to actuate the trash flap,
a visible light source configured to emit visible light; and
the multiple light sources include:[[an ]]multiple ultraviolet light sources configured to emit ultraviolet light having a wavelength that at least one of injures, neutralizes, or kills pathogens.
12. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 11, wherein the central controller is further configured to control each of the multiple actuators[[ or]] and the multiple light sources to cause a total power draw of the system to remain at or below a power threshold corresponding to a maximum amount of power available to the system.
13. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 11, wherein the central controller is further configured to determine a health status of the system including at least one of a remaining life of the multiple ultraviolet light sources, surface wear experienced by surfaces of the lavatory in response to the ultraviolet light, or a remaining quantity of supplies in the lavatory, and to control at least one of the multiple actuators or light sources further based on the health status.
14. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 10, wherein the inference includes at least one of an inferred portion of the lavatory used by a passenger for which sanitization is desirable or whether the lavatory is occupied.
15. (Currently Amended) A method for touchless control of a lavatory of an aircraft, the method comprising:detecting receiving, by at least one sensor of the lavatory, detected data corresponding to the lavatory;
making, by a central controller, an inference as to a portion of the lavatory that was used and for which sanitation is desirable based on the detected data received; and
controlling, by the central controller, at least one actuator or at least one light source of the lavatory based on the inference.
16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 15, wherein the at least one sensor includes multiple sensors, and wherein the at least one actuator or light source includes the at least one actuator and the at least one light source.
17. (Original) The method of claim 16, wherein the central controller is further configured to control the at least one actuator and the at least one light source to cause a total power draw of the lavatory to remain at or below a power threshold corresponding to a maximum amount of power available to the lavatory.
18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17, wherein the central controller is further configured to control the at least one actuator and the at least one light source to operate sequentially to cause the total power draw of the system to remain at or below the power threshold.
19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 16, further comprising determining, by the central controller, a health status of the system including at least one of a remaining life of the at least one light source, surface wear experienced by surfaces of the lavatory in response to light emitted by the at least one light source, or a remaining quantity of supplies in the lavatory,
wherein controlling the at least one actuator or the at least one light source includes controlling the at least one actuator or the at least one light source further based on the health status.
20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 15, wherein the inference includes at least one of an inferred portion of the lavatory used by a passenger for which sanitization is desirable or whether the lavatory is occupied.
